To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sera of 66% of DLE patients inhibit the interaction of DNA with hexamminecobalt (III) chloride.
The sera of patients with D.L.E. contain a factor that inhibits the hexammine cobaltic chloride clot test for DNA.

the sera of 66% of DLE patients inhibit clotting by hexamminecobalt(III) chloride of calf thymu DNA, that such inhibition is removed from sera by prior incubation of sera with calf thymus nuclei, and that such inhibition is prevented by addition of histone to normal sera or by prior treatment of calf thymn DNA with DNase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the serum factor which inhibits the hexamminecobalt(III) chloride clotting of calf thymu s DNA.
the study of the serum inhibitor of DNA-hex-amminecobalt(III) complex formation.
the interaction of DNA with hexamminecobalt chloride and the effects of sera of patients with disseminated lupus erythematosus (DLE) and normal sera on such interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the serum factor inhibiting hexamminecobalt chloride-DNA clot formation in patients with DLE is a nucleoprotein complex, which is probably a DNA-protein complex.
the serum factor inhibiting the DNA-cobalt interaction is a DNA-binding protein which is not histone or protaminelike, and which is removed from the sera by nuclear proteins.
the serum factor responsible for inhibition of hexamminecobalt chloride, DNA clot formation in DLE is a DNA binding protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a serum inhibitor of hexammine cobaltic chloride, DNA interaction, is present in the sera of patients with D LE, but not in normal sera.
a serum factor, present in the sera of 66% of the patients with DLE, inhibits the interaction of hexamminecobalt chloride with calf thymus deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA).

a serum factor, which is present in the sera of approximately two-thirds of patients with disseminated lupus erythematosus (DLE), inhibits the grossly visible interaction between hexamminecobalt chloride and calf thymus (CT) DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inhibition of DNA interaction by sera of patients with D LE is a nonspecific phenomenon and that this inhibition is due to a component of the sera that can be removed by incubation with whole nuclei or DNA.
the inhibition of hexamminecobalt DNA interaction by sera from patients with DLE may be related to the presence of a nuclear protein in such sera.
the serum of DLE patients contains an inhibiting factor which is removed by prior exposure to DNA and/or DNA-protein complexes.
